latest_apis.rationale: Every API in the app is on the current stable SolidStart v2 stack, including the 2.1.0 patch released eight days ago; it deliberately avoids the Solid 2 / router 2 RCs. I verified each pattern against the v2 docs (data-fetching, createHandler, HttpStatusCode, head/metadata, deployment plugins) and found no v1-era remnants.

platform.rationale: The app reaches for the platform first everywhere: fetch, URLSearchParams, native form controls, CSS custom properties and logical properties, lazy/async image decoding. No polyfills, no utility library standing in for platform features. The only platform gap is that no fetch carries an AbortController/timeout.

dependencies.rationale: As lean as a SolidStart app can be: every dependency is one the official v2 setup installs, and everything else is hand-rolled from platform primitives. Only nit: vite and nitro are build-time-only and could sit in devDependencies, though the official docs install them as regular deps.

churn_resistance.rationale: Framework or requirements changes would touch very few files — data access, config and repeated markup are each behind one module, and nothing depends on internals. It falls short of a 5 because the upstream PokeAPI layer is typed as `any` throughout model.ts and query-string parsing is duplicated between preload and component, so upstream changes fail at runtime rather than in the type checker.

findings.issue: Upstream PokeAPI responses are typed `any` (TypeInfo.detail, the (a: any, b: any) stat/ability sorts, move/type maps), and api<T = any> in pokeapi.ts:36 defaults to any, so a change in the API's shape becomes a silent runtime rendering bug rather than a compile error.
findings.suggestion: Define minimal interfaces for the handful of PokeAPI resources actually consumed (NamedAPIResource, Pokemon, Species, Move, Type, Ability, Generation) in lib/server/pokeapi.ts and make api<T> require an explicit T; the view models in types.ts already provide the typed boundary on the other side.

findings.issue: process.env.API_BASE_URL is read directly, which ties the server module to the Node preset; Nitro v3's portable mechanism is runtimeConfig (set via the nitro property in vite.config.ts), and process.env is not reliably available on edge/serverless presets.
findings.suggestion: Expose apiBase via nitro.runtimeConfig in vite.config.ts and read it with useRuntimeConfig() in pokeapi.ts, so switching deployment presets needs no code change.

findings.issue: No fetch carries a timeout or AbortSignal, so a hung PokeAPI call stalls the request forever and permanently occupies one of the 24 semaphore slots.
findings.suggestion: Pass AbortSignal.timeout(10_000) to fetch and treat aborts like the existing NotFoundError path.

findings.issue: Query-string parsing/serialization is written twice — filtersFrom/searchFor in the component (and the URLSearchParams version inside preload at :46-49), and gameParam duplicated in pokemon/[name].tsx:13 and :28 — so a new filter must be added in several places.
findings.suggestion: Move filtersFrom/searchFor into lib/format.ts (or a small lib/searchParams.ts) and have the route's preload import the same helpers.

findings.issue: The pure helpers most likely to be touched by a refactor (humanize, dexNumber, display, and the missing-values-last comparator in MoveTable.tsx:31-40) have no unit tests; app/ contains zero test files.
findings.suggestion: Add a couple of focused tests for format.ts and the MoveTable sort comparator — they are pure, cheap to cover, and encode spec rules (em dash, #0025, Mr Mime).

summary: This is a textbook SolidStart v2 app: deps pinned to the current stable stack (start 2.1.0, router 1.0.0, vite 8, nitro 3) released days before today, the exact query/createAsync/preload and createHandler patterns from the v2 docs, and a lean six-dependency footprint with zero utility libraries. Data access, configuration and repeated markup are each isolated behind one module, so framework or requirements changes would ripple very little. The one thing I'd ask for in review is a typed layer for the upstream PokeAPI responses, which are `any` throughout model.ts and would fail at runtime rather than at compile time.

apis.replacement: Works on the Node preset and is not deprecated, but Nitro v3's portable equivalent is runtimeConfig + useRuntimeConfig()
